title: Cap. V Obj. 7: without foresight-faith condition the whole Gospel is inverted
latin: Obj. 7. Si electio non ponatur ex antecedanea fidei praevisae conditione, tum Evangelium totum invertitur. Nam cum Evangelium prius mandet fidem, deinde sub conditione fidei salutem promittat, doctrina eorum qui Arminio repugnant, ponit Deum primo alicui personae singulari ordinasse salutem, deinde vero fidem. Evangelium dicit, Crede, et vives: haec vero doctrina dicit, Quoniam tibi volo dare vitam, propterea tibi volo dare fidem, quae est ipsissima Evangelii eversio. Concedenda ergo electio ex praevisae fidei conditione, aut Evangelii doctrina explodenda est.
pass_a: Objection 7. If election is not put from an antecedent condition of foresight faith, then the whole Gospel is inverted. For since the Gospel first commands faith, then under the condition of faith promises salvation, the doctrine of those who resist Arminius puts God as having first ordained salvation to some singular person, then truly faith. The Gospel says, Believe, and you will live: but this doctrine says, Because I will to give you life, therefore I will to give you faith, which is the very overturning of the Gospel. Election from the condition of foresight faith is therefore to be conceded, or the doctrine of the Gospel is to be exploded.
pass_b: Obj. 7. If election is not set from an antecedent condition of foresight faith, the whole Gospel is inverted. The Gospel first commands faith, then under that condition promises salvation — but those who resist Arminius have God first ordaining salvation to a singular person, then faith. The Gospel says, Believe and you will live; their doctrine says, Because I will to give you life, therefore I will to give you faith — the very overturning of the Gospel. So concede election from a foresight-faith condition, or explode Gospel doctrine.

title: Cap. V Obj. 7 Sol: secret decree Rom. 9 — in God no prior/posterior decrees; order of causes
latin: Sol. Respondeo, Modo concedatur arcanum illud decretum Dei, cujus vult miseretur, et quem vult duritiae suae innatae relinquentes, Jacobum diligentis, Esavum odio habentis, idque ante omnem considerationem bene aut male factorum in iisdem, nos de ordine prioritatis et posterioritatis in decreto aeternae vitae et efficacis gratiae quoad ipsos praedestinatos, ne tantillum quidem laborare. Nam scimus in Deo quoad rem non esse decreta alia aliis priora aut posteriora: quoad modum autem considerationis nostrae et rerum inter se habitudinem idem decretum alteri comparatum potest eo et prius et posterius esse, secundum diversum ordinem causarum. Sic decretum dandi fidem in ordine causae efficientis prius est quam dandi vitam: decretum dandi vitam in ordine causae finalis prius est quam dandi fidem.
pass_a: Solution. I answer, Provided that secret decree of God be conceded, of him whose he wills he has mercy, and whom he wills leaving to their innate hardness, loving Jacob, having Esau in hatred, and that before all consideration of things well or ill done in the same, we labor not even a little about the order of priority and posteriority in the decree of eternal life and of efficacious grace as to the predestinated themselves. For we know that in God as to the thing there are not decrees some prior or posterior to others: but as to the mode of our consideration and the mutual habitude of things the same decree compared to another can be both prior and posterior to it, according to a diverse order of causes. Thus the decree of giving faith in the order of efficient cause is prior to that of giving life: the decree of giving life in the order of final cause is prior to that of giving faith.
pass_b: Sol. I answer: grant that secret decree of God who has mercy on whom he wills and leaves whom he wills to their innate hardness — loving Jacob, hating Esau, before any consideration of their good or evil deeds — and we do not labor even a little over priority and posteriority in the decree of eternal life and efficacious grace as to the predestinated. In God as to the thing, decrees are not prior or posterior to each other; as to our mode of considering and the mutual relation of things, the same decree compared to another can be both prior and posterior by a diverse order of causes. So the decree to give faith is prior in the order of efficient cause to giving life; the decree to give life is prior in the order of final cause to giving faith.

lemmas.gloss: secret decree loving Jacob, hating Esau

title: Cap. V Obj. 7 Sol: Biel — end loved before means; faith gift prepared with life destinated
latin: Recte enim Biel, Prius diligitur finis quam medium, quod propter finem diligitur: quia dilectio finis est aliquo modo causa dilectionis eorum omnium quae sunt ad finem. Cum enim fides sit donum Dei, vitam aeternam credenti apportans, quis audeat dicere hoc donum fuisse Petro aut Paulo praeparatum et donatum, vita aeterna nondum illis destinata? quasi Deus beneficium, quod ex suo dono orietur, non destinaverit ei, quem eodem dono prae aliis voluerit locupletare.
pass_a: For Biel rightly, The end is loved before the means, which is loved on account of the end: because the love of the end is in some way the cause of the love of all those things which are unto the end. For since faith is a gift of God, bringing eternal life to the believer, who would dare say that this gift was prepared and gifted to Peter or Paul, eternal life not yet destinated to them? as if God had not destinated the benefit which will arise from his gift to him whom he willed to enrich with the same gift before others.
pass_b: Biel is right: the end is loved before the means loved for the end's sake — love of the end is in some way cause of loving all that is unto the end. Since faith is God's gift bringing eternal life to the believer, who would dare say that gift was prepared and given to Peter or Paul while eternal life was not yet destinated to them? As if God had not destinated the benefit arising from his gift to the one he willed to enrich with that gift before others.

title: Cap. V Obj. 7 Sol: Gospel not inverted — Quisquis crediderit; elect get constant faith
latin: Sed accedamus propius ad rationem propositam. Negamus ex sententia nostra Evangelium inverti, aut quicquam Evangelio adversum in ea contineri. Evangelium dicit, Quisquis crediderit, salvus erit: Nos dicimus, Deum ex speciali misericordia quibusdam, quos infallibiliter ad vitam perducere decrevit, fidem constantem inspirare. Evangelium prius mandat fidem, deinde sub conditione fidei salutem promittit: Nos docemus, Deum primo ordinare singularem aliquam personam ad vitam, deinde vero fidem cordi ejusdem infundere. Ego pugnam aut contradictionem hic nullam invenio. Vox Evangelizantis instituit singulos, quibus modis et mediis possint vitam aeternam consequi: Media igitur sub conditione praemittit, quibus reis consecutionem promittit. At decretum Dei eligentis praestituit certis personis et media et finem, finem per media, et media propter finem; atque idcirco dicitur finem prius et principalius respicere, quia propter infallibilem ejus adeptionem talem gratiam concipitur tali personae praeparare.
pass_a: But let us come nearer to the reason proposed. We deny that from our position the Gospel is inverted, or that anything adverse to the Gospel is contained in it. The Gospel says, Whoever shall have believed will be saved: We say that God from special mercy inspires constant faith in certain ones whom he has decreed to lead through infallibly to life. The Gospel first commands faith, then under the condition of faith promises salvation: We teach that God first ordains some singular person to life, then truly pours faith into the heart of the same. I find here no fight or contradiction. The voice of the one evangelizing instructs individuals by what modes and means they may obtain eternal life: It therefore puts means first under a condition, to those who use which it promises the attainment. But the decree of God electing prefizes for certain persons both means and end, the end through means, and the means on account of the end; and therefore it is said to look to the end first and more principally, because on account of its infallible attainment such grace is conceived as prepared for such a person.
pass_b: Nearer then to their reason. We deny that our position inverts the Gospel or holds anything against it. The Gospel says Whoever believes will be saved; we say God from special mercy inspires constant faith in certain ones he has decreed to lead infallibly to life. The Gospel first commands faith, then under that condition promises salvation; we teach God first ordains a singular person to life, then pours faith into that heart. I find no fight or contradiction here. The evangelizing voice tells individuals by what means they may obtain eternal life — it puts means first under a condition and promises attainment to those who use them. But God's electing decree prefizes for certain persons both means and end — end through means, means for the end — and so is said to look to the end first and more principally, because for its infallible attainment such grace is conceived as prepared for that person.

lemmas.gloss: means and end prefized for the elect

title: Cap. V Obj. 7 Sol close: Augustine on perseverance; God requires faith then gifts it to the elect
latin: Nullam hic contradictionem invenire potuit Augustinus, qui optime novit hanc esse Evangelii doctrinam, Quisquis ad finem usque perseveraverit, salvus erit; et tamen ipse docuit, Sanctis in regnum Dei ante jacta mundi fundamenta praedestinatis hanc ipsam perseverantiam praeparatam et donatam. Ut brevi absolvam; Nulla in hisce duobus effatis pugna est, Deus primo a nobis exigit officia fidei, deinde promittit beneficium vitae: et Deus, quoniam pro speciali sua misericordia quosdam elegit ad participandum vitae aeternae beneficium, propterea vult illis efficaciter fidem dare, ut impleant hoc officium.
pass_a: Augustine could find no contradiction here, who best knew that this is the doctrine of the Gospel, Whoever shall have persevered even to the end will be saved; and yet he himself taught that to the saints predestinated into the kingdom of God before the foundations of the world were laid, this very perseverance was prepared and gifted. That I may finish briefly; There is no fight in these two sayings, God first exacts from us the duties of faith, then promises the benefit of life: and God, since for his special mercy he has elected certain ones to share in the benefit of eternal life, therefore wills to give them faith efficaciously, that they may fulfill this duty.
pass_b: Augustine found no contradiction here — he knew best that Gospel doctrine is Whoever perseveres to the end will be saved, yet taught that to saints predestinated into God's kingdom before the world's foundations this very perseverance was prepared and gifted. Briefly: these two sayings do not fight — God first exacts from us the duties of faith, then promises the benefit of life; and because for his special mercy he elected certain ones to share eternal life's benefit, he therefore wills to give them faith efficaciously so they may fulfill that duty.

lemmas.gloss: exact faith-duty; gift faith to elect
